title: How to Earn Qantas Status
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Earn status credits to climb your way to Qantas Silver, Gold, Platinum and Platinum One status.
Qantas Frequent Flyer status is the gateway to a more enjoyable travel experience with Qantas and its partner airlines.
Earn Qantas status and you’ll enjoy perks like lounge access, bonus points, higher Qantas upgrade priority , extra baggage allowance and many more benefits! You’ll also be able to skip the airport queues with access to priority check-in, security and boarding lanes.
Platinum frequent flyers can access Qantas international First Class lounges. Photo: Qantas.
Every Qantas Frequent Flyer member starts out at the Bronze tier. To earn Qantas status, you’ll need to accumulate enough status credits and take at least 4 Qantas or Jetstar flights during your personal membership year. This membership year is based on the month when you originally joined the program.
Status credits are completely separate to Qantas Frequent Flyer points. Points are the loyalty program’s reward currency and can be redeemed for things like reward flights, upgrades and hotel bookings. Status credits, on the other hand, help you climb to a higher status tier within the program. And as we’ll explain in this mega guide, there are a few shortcuts to earn status credits faster!
It’s not possible to buy Qantas status credits . You have to earn them – generally by flying with Qantas, Jetstar or Oneworld partner airlines. Your Qantas status credits balance will reset to zero at the end of each membership year.
The benefits of Qantas Frequent Flyer status
There are four Qantas Frequent Flyer status tiers:
Silver
Gold
Platinum
Platinum One
Each tier comes with increased benefits.
When you earn status with Qantas, you’ll also receive reciprocal status benefits with Oneworld airlines . Qantas Silver , Gold and Platinum is equivalent to Oneworld Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald status, respectively. This means your loyalty will also be recognised when flying with Oneworld airlines including Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, Malaysia Airlines and British Airways.
Oneworld member airlines.
Qantas Frequent Flyer Silver (Oneworld Ruby) tier benefits
Upon reaching Qantas Silver status, you’ll receive benefits including:
50% bonus points on Qantas, Jetstar & American Airlines flights
An annual Qantas lounge invitation (increasing to two annual invitations in 2027)
Extra baggage allowance
Priority check-in
Free seat selection on all Qantas international flights (seat selection is free anyway on bookings within or departing Australia)
See our Guide to Qantas Silver Status for more details.

Qantas Frequent Flyer Gold (Oneworld Sapphire) benefits
The benefits really start to add up once you reach Gold status. Key benefits include:
75% bonus points on Qantas, Jetstar & American Airlines flights
Complimentary Qantas Club and International Business Lounge access
Priority access to Qantas Classic Flight Reward seats (particularly in premium cabins on Qantas international flights)
Priority boarding (in Group 2 on selected domestic flights )
Priority baggage
Complimentary access to Economy Plus seats after online check-in opens
See our Guide to Qantas Gold Status for more information.
The Qantas Club at Karratha Airport. Photo: Qantas.
Qantas Frequent Flyer Platinum (Oneworld Emerald) benefits
Key additional benefits of Qantas Platinum status include:
100% bonus points on Qantas, Jetstar & American Airlines flights
Qantas Domestic Business Lounge access (with up to two guests, instead of one)
International First Lounge access
Access to Qantas domestic lounges on arrival at your destination
Priority boarding Group 1 on selected Qantas domestic flights
Complimentary Economy Plus seats
Qantas Economy Plus seats have extra legroom. Photo: Qantas.
There are also a few unpublished benefits of Qantas Platinum status:
The ability to request the release of additional Classic Flight Reward seats
Less wait time when phoning the Qantas call centre (and are more likely to get the wonderful Hobart call centre)
On international flights, you might get a personal welcome from the Customer Service Manager (this also happens when flying some partner airlines such as Cathay Pacific and Emirates)
You can read more in our article about the perks of Qantas Platinum status .
Qantas Platinum One perks
For high flyers, additional Platinum One benefits include:
Gift Platinum status to a family member or friend
Two complimentary Business/First Lounge invitations to gift
Qantas VIP Service Team support
Highest upgrade priority and confirmed international flight upgrades 2-7 days before departure on Qantas flights
Access to up-front seats from the time of booking on Qantas flights
Many service fees are waived
Invitations to special events
While this is not guaranteed, some Platinum One members receive occasional free upgrades and invitations to the Chairman’s Lounge
You can read more about the benefits of Platinum One status – and whether it’s worth it – on the Australian Frequent Flyer forum .
Platinum and Platinum One frequent flyers can use the Qantas First Lounge. Photo: Qantas.
You’ll find a full list of tier benefits on the Qantas website .
How to reach a higher Qantas Frequent Flyer tier
This table shows the number of Qantas status credits and minimum flights required per membership year to qualify for or renew Qantas Frequent Flyer status:
To earn or renew Platinum One status, there is an additional requirement that you earn at least 2,700 status credits from Qantas marketed flights.
Sometime in 2027, Qantas will increase the “retain” thresholds to match the “earn” thresholds for Silver, Gold and Platinum status . The airline has not yet revealed the exact date when this will happen.
How to earn Qantas status credits from flying
You can earn status credits when flying on any Qantas marketed flight (i.e. when booked on a “QF” flight number), regardless of the operating airline.
You can also earn status credits when flying with any Oneworld airline, provided the flight is both marketed and operated by a Oneworld carrier.
Earn status credits flying with other Oneworld airlines, including Finnair. Photo: Adobe Stock.
Earning Qantas status credits on Jetstar
You can also earn Qantas status credits on Jetstar, but only under the following circumstances:
If you’ve purchased a Jetstar Flex, Flex Plus or Business Max Bundle with your ticket
If you have a Club Jetstar membership with a Qantas Frequent Flyer Extra subscription
If you’re flying on a Qantas codeshare with a “QF” flight number.
Only Jetstar flights with a Plus or Max bundle earn status credits or count as eligible sectors. Photo: Jetstar.
How many Qantas status credits do you earn per flight?
The number of Qantas status credits you’ll earn per flight depends on three things:
The route
The marketing airline
The fare class you’ve booked
In general, you’ll earn more status credits for booking longer flights and more expensive tickets. For example, you’ll earn 10 status credits on a cheap Qantas Red e-Deal Economy ticket from Melbourne to Sydney. But you’d earn 20 status credits with a Flexible Economy ticket or 40 status credits for Business Class on the same route.
On a longer flight, such as Sydney to London , you would earn 70 status credits on a cheap Economy Sale fare or as many as 420 status credits each way if travelling in First Class.
